'''Zillennials''', occasionally called '''Zennials''', are a social [[Cohort (statistics)|cohort]] encompassing people [[Cusper|born on the cusp of]] or during the later years of the [[Millennials|Millennial]] generation and the early years of [[Generation Z]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The American Generations: Names, Years, & Key Differences {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Experience-the-American-Generations-Which-Generation-Are-You-2226598 |access-date=2 September 2025 |website=www.britannica.com |language=en}}</ref> Sources typically give ranges of those born from 1993 to 1998, though some extend this further in either direction. Their adjacency between the two generations and limited [[age set]] has led to their characterization as a "micro-generation".<ref name="Cheong2023">{{Cite web |last=Cheong |first=Charissa |title=How to spot a 'zillennial' in the wild, according to TikTok |url=https://www.insider.com/spotting-zillennials-millenial-gen-z-tiktok-2023-7 |access-date=25 August 2023 |website=Insider |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Zennials">{{cite book |author1=Hannah L. Ubl |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pZuqDgAAQBAJ |title=Managing Millennials For Dummies |author2=Lisa X. Walden |author3=Debra Arbit |date=24 April 2017 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-1-119-31022-8 |page=266 |chapter=Chapter 13: Making Adjustments for Ages and Life Stages}}</ref> They are generally the children of [[Generation Jones|younger Baby Boomers]] and [[Generation X]].<ref name="UblWalden2017" /> Estimates of the [[Demographics of the United States|US population]] in this cohort range from 30 million to 48&nbsp;million.<ref name=":8"/><ref name=":7" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Samuel |first1=Sturgeon |title=A Snapshot Of Millennial Births |url=https://ifstudies.org/blog/a-snapshot-of-millennial-births |website=Institute of Family Studies |access-date=19 January 2019}}</ref> <!-- Please discuss the inclusion of a date range in the lede on the talk page.-->

== Etymology ==
The term ''Zillennial'' is a [[Blend word|portmanteau]] of "Generation Z" and "Millennial".<ref name="Reflectdigital">{{Cite web |title=Zillennials: The Widely Unrecognised Microgeneration |url=https://www.reflectdigital.co.uk/blog/zillennials-the-widely-unrecognised-microgeneration |access-date=12 July 2025 |website=Reflect Digital |language=en}}</ref> A similar portmanteau, ''Zennial'', is also used,<ref name="DeGering2021">{{cite web |last1=DeGering |first1=Nicea |date=4 March 2021 |title=Do you feel left out of the generational war? You might be a zennial |url=https://www.abc4.com/gtu/do-you-feel-left-out-of-the-generational-war-you-might-be-a-zennial/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305023044/https://www.abc4.com/gtu/do-you-feel-left-out-of-the-generational-war-you-might-be-a-zennial/ |archive-date=5 March 2021 |access-date=7 March 2021 |website=abc4.com}}</ref> which is comparable to ''[[Xennials]]'' (a portmanteau of [[Generation X]] and [[Millennials]]). Other names that have been proposed for these cuspers include the ''[[Snapchat]] Generation'' by authors Ubl, Walden, and Arbit,<ref name="UblWalden2017">{{cite book |first1=Hannah L.|last1=Ubl |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pZuqDgAAQBAJ |title=Managing Millennials For Dummies |first2=Lisa X.|last2=Walden |first3=Debra|last3=Arbit |date=24 April 2017 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-1-119-31022-8 |page=266 |chapter=Chapter 13: Making Adjustments for Ages and Life Stages}}</ref> and ''MinionZ'' by Smit.<ref name="Smit2017">{{cite journal |last=Smit |first=Deon |date=December 2017 |title=Do you have enough "Generational Glue" in your organisation? |url=https://journals.co.za/content/journal/10520/EJC-b978fc1a0 |journal=HR Future |volume=2017 |issue=Dec 2017 |pages=22–23 |issn=1608-8506}}</ref> ''GenZennials'' was used to reference the micro-generation by [[Ketchum Inc.|Ketchum]].<ref name=":1">{{cite press release | url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/ketchum-introduces-the-genzennial-an-influential-blend-of-two-generations-300429599.html | title=Ketchum Introduces the GenZennial, an Influential Blend of Two Generations }}</ref>

== Date and age range definitions ==<!-- Please do NOT change the date ranges without adding new and reliable sources.-->

The exact date range of this micro-generation is not specifically defined, but encompasses the latter years of the Millennial generation and the early years of Generation Z. [[Pew Research Center]] stated that "the differences within generations can be just as great as the differences across generations, and the youngest and oldest within a commonly defined cohort may feel more in common with bordering generations than the one to which they are assigned."<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2019/01/17/where-millennials-end-and-generation-z-begins/ | title=Defining generations: Where Millennials end and Generation Z begins | date=17 January 2019 }}</ref>

''[[Dictionary.com]]'' defines "zillennial" as a person born between the early 1990s and late 1990s.<ref>{{cite web |title=ZILLENNIAL Definition & Meaning {{!}} Dictionary.com |url=https://www.dictionary.com/browse/zillennial |access-date=2026-06-20 |website=www.dictionary.com}}</ref> Charissa Cheong, writing for ''[[Business Insider]]'', defines Zillennials as "born roughly between 1990 and 2000".<ref name="Cheong2023" /> Payment processing researcher PYMNTS defines Zillennials as those born from 1991 to 1999.<ref>{{cite report |title=52 Mondays: The Weekly Guide to the Connected Economy |url=https://www.pymnts.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/2024-12-eBook-52-Mondays.pdf |publisher=PYMNTS Intelligence |date=December 2024 |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Zillennial Paradox: Big Debt, Big Spending and a Conscience to Rule It All |url=https://www.pymnts.com/study_posts/the-zillennial-paradox-big-debt-big-spending-and-a-conscience-to-rule-it-all/ |website=PYMNTS |date=May 2024 |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=41% of Zillennials Prioritize Price Over Brand Loyalty in Shopping |url=https://www.pymnts.com/consumer-insights/2024/41percent-of-zillennials-prioritize-price-over-brand-loyalty-in-shopping/ |website=PYMNTS |date=11 November 2024 |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> Authors Hannah Ubl, Lisa Walden, and Debra Arbit define the cuspers as those born between 1992 and 1998,<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=g36gDgAAQBAJ&dq=ubl+walden+arbit+1992-1998&pg=PA266 | isbn=978-1-119-31023-5 | title=Managing Millennials for Dummies | date=6 April 2017 | publisher=John Wiley & Sons }}</ref> as does Mary Everett (''[[PopSugar]]),''<ref name="Everett">{{cite web |last=Everett |first=Mary |date=3 March 2021 |title=Are You Confused by the Current Generational War? Congrats, You May Be a Zennial! |url=https://www.popsugar.com/smart-living/what-are-zennials-48195753 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303231903/https://www.popsugar.com/smart-living/what-are-zennials-48195753 |archive-date=3 March 2021 |access-date=8 March 2021 |website=PopSugar}}</ref> Nicea DeGering ([[KTVX]]),<ref>{{cite web |last=DeGering |first=Nicea |title=Do you feel left out of the generational war? You might be a zennial |url=https://www.abc4.com/gtu/do-you-feel-left-out-of-the-generational-war-you-might-be-a-zennial/ |website=ABC4 Utah |access-date=19 February 2026 |date=4 March 2021}}</ref> and a [[WGSN (trend forecasting)|WGSN]] case study.<ref name="Napoli2020">{{cite web |last1=Napoli |first1=Cassandra |date=22 May 2020 |title=WGSN: Zennials: The In-Between Generation |url=https://www.wgsn.com/insight/p/article/88103?lang=en |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201025231640/https://www.wgsn.com/insight/p/article/88103?lang=en |archive-date=25 October 2020 |access-date=18 February 2021 |website=wgsn.com}}</ref> [[Boston University]] sociologist [[Deborah Carr]] defines zillennials as those born "roughly" between 1992 and 2002, but notes that "there isn't one consistent cutoff point that experts agree on".<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Ward |first=Terry |date=10 May 2023 |title=Zillennials: The newest micro-generation has a name |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/05/10/health/what-are-zillennials-wellness/index.html |website=CNN}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Zillennials: A new name for a generation – CBS Chicago | website=[[CBS News]] | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/video/zillennials-a-new-name-for-a-generation/ }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Kaufman |first1=Anna |title=Move over Millennials and Gen Z, there's a new generation in town: Meet Zillennials |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/2023/05/18/is-zillennial-a-real-thing/70207436007/ |website=USA TODAY |access-date=19 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3_O2bHknIzE |title=Zillennials: A new micro-generation {{!}} The Hill |date=11 May 2023 |last=NewsNation |access-date=19 February 2026 |via=YouTube}}</ref> 

Others have defined zillennials as those born from 1993 to 1998, including ''[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=The American Generations: Names, Years, & Key Differences {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Experience-the-American-Generations-Which-Generation-Are-You-2226598 |access-date=21 February 2024 |website=www.britannica.com |language=en}}</ref> Deon Smit (''HR Future''),<ref name="Smit2017" /> Maisy Farren (''[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]''),<ref name="Farren2020">{{Cite web |last1=Farren |first1=Maisy |date=20 August 2020 |title='Zillennials' Are Haunted By Their Internet History |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/zillennials-are-haunted-by-their-internet-history/ |access-date=15 October 2020 |website=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]] |language=en}}</ref> Lindsay Dodgson (''[[Business Insider]]''),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dodgson |first=Lindsay |title=The struggle of being a workplace 'zillennial,' not knowing where you fit in |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/zillennials-are-caught-between-generations-in-the-workplace-2024-10 |access-date=19 November 2025 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> Charlotte Hilton Andersen and Jason Dorsey (''[[Reader's Digest]]''),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andersen |first=Charlotte Hilton |date=30 May 2025 |title=What Generation Are You? == Characteristics ==
Zillennials are influenced by traits of both the preceding Millennial generation and subsequent Generation Z, often sharing strong, polarizing connectivity to one adjoining generation over the other.<ref name=":2">{{cite web |title=WGSN: Zennials: The In-Between Generation – WGSN Insight |url=https://www.wgsn.com/insight/p/article/88103?lang=en#page8 |access-date=25 August 2023 |website=www.wgsn.com |quote=Zennials are very opinionated about where they stand on this spectrum and have showed strong preferences.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Joshi |first=Shamani |date=31 May 2021 |title=What It's Like To Be a Zillennial, the Generation Caught Between Gen Z and Millennials |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/generation-betwen-genz-and-millennials-zillennials/ |access-date=25 August 2023 |website=Vice |language=en}}</ref> Members of this micro-generation consider the "fluid" nature of their [[age grade]] unsettling with potential to "tarnish their status and input in the workplace [via [[ageism]]]", according to a [[WGSN (trend forecasting)|WGSN]] case study.<ref name=":2" /> The case study found that some zillennials preferred to be seen as Millennials in the workplace, as they are seen as more professional, while younger zillennials believed they were "too young" for the characterization.<ref name="Napoli2020" /> According to author Tim Elmore, social scientists believe that a second micro-generation could lie between the Millennial generation and Generation Z due to rapid demographic change during the 2010s.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UX9zEAAAQBAJ&q=microgenerations|title=A New Kind of Diversity: Making the Different Generations on Your Team a Competitive Advantage|first=Tim|last=Elmore|date=25 October 2022|publisher=Simon and Schuster|isbn=9798887100012 |accessdate=7 August 2023|via=Google Books}}</ref>

A 2024 survey conducted by [[YouGov]] among 13,083 US adults found that 31 percent of Millennials relate to their own generation the most, while 19 percent relate to Gen Z. On the other hand, 31 percent of Gen Zers relate to their own generation the most, while 15 percent relate to Millennials. The survey also found that most Millennials and Gen Zers do not consider themselves to be part of the generation they're officially a part of.<ref>{{cite web |title=Most Millennials and Gen Zers don't place themselves within their usual generational group {{!}} YouGov |url=https://today.yougov.com/society/articles/48956-most-millennials-gen-zers-dont-place-themselves-within-usual-generational-group-poll |access-date=17 September 2025 |website=today.yougov.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

Members of this cohort were children in the 2000s, during events such as the [[September 11 attacks|9/11 terrorist attacks]].<ref name="Napoli2020" /> Zillennials were too young for full understanding of the geopolitical context or the gravity of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, but grew up in [[Aftermath of the September 11 attacks|the significant aftermath]] that helped shape their worldview. They came of age in the 2010s, with the [[2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum|Brexit referendum]] and [[2016 United States presidential election|US presidential election]] of 2016, [[COVID-19 pandemic]], and the [[George Floyd protests|2020–2021 George Floyd protests]] being key formative events.<ref name="Napoli2020" /> They remember life in the early 2000s before [[smartphone]]s,<ref name="Reflectdigital"/> then experienced the sudden global [[Digital Revolution]] of the late 2000s and 2010s, navigating mobile [[LTE (telecommunication)|LTE internet]], cell phones, mobile devices, and smartphones.<ref name="Everett" />

Zillennials [[Code-switching|code-switch]] between generations,<ref name=":5" /> have high levels of [[digital literacy]],<ref name=":4" /> and are more likely to self-identify into a minority group.<ref name="Dreisinger2019" /> They are less wealthy but more [[Job security|economically secure]] than Generation Z, commanding relatively high spending power in the [[Economy of the United States|US economy]], especially when compared to Millennials.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":6" /> They also have high [[brand loyalty]], low [[Price elasticity of demand|price sensitivity]], and stable purchasing patterns.

Maddy Mussen, writing for ''[[Evening Standard|The Standard]]'', said that zillennials "have a unique position of being close enough to Gen Z that we can understand their strange language and behaviours, but with enough years behind us that our behaviour hasn’t been totally and irrevocably warped by the forces that f***ed up their youth. We were on the last helicopter out of TikTok-gon." She also stated that zillennials grew up in a world shaped "for the better" by Millennials, "[[body positivity]], [[Sex-positive movement|sex positivity]], and [[fourth-wave feminism]] were all reaching a peak during our formative years."<ref>https://www.standard.co.uk/lifestyle/zillennial-gen-z-lazy-normal-b1241772.html</ref>

Zillennials are seen as a bridge between the digital pioneers of the early internet (Millennials) and the "internet natives" of Gen Z according to a definition made by [[Trusted Media Brands]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Zillennials: the influential, in-between generation driving engagement across our platforms. {{!}} TMB (Trusted Media Brands) posted on the topic {{!}} LinkedIn |url=https://www.linkedin.com/posts/trusted-media-brands-inc-_zillennials-audiencediscovery-audienceinsights-activity-7323096255113416704-hpQ3 |access-date=12 August 2025 |website=www.linkedin.com |language=en}}</ref>

Jason Dorsey, president of The Center for Generational Kinetics, described zillennials as "equal parts idealistic and skeptical, analog roots with digital instincts" and that "they probably remember life before smartphones, but not before the internet".<ref>{{cite web |last=Dorsey |first=Jason |date=17 June 2025 |title=Jason Dorsey Featured in Reader's Digest on Generational Identity |url=https://jasondorsey.com/blog/featured-in-readers-digest-on-generational-identity/ |access-date=26 September 2025 |website=Jason Dorsey |language=en-GB}}</ref>

According to authors Trompenaars and Woolliams, zillennials "were born digital and do not know a world without social media or the internet. They don't consider they have a born right to owning property with a mortgage or a career where they have the same job at the beginning and end of their working life. They like sharing their feelings with friends".<ref>{{cite book |last1=Trompenaars |first1=Fons |last2=Woolliams |first2=Peter |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=f8rvEAAAQBAJ&dq=zillennials+micro+generation&pg=PA38 |title=New Approaches to Recruitment and Selection |date=29 January 2024 |publisher=Emerald Group Publishing |isbn=978-1-83797-759-8 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Arts and culture ===
The advent of "Zillennialcore" to describe the cultural backdrop of this micro-generation references music, media, and fashion.<ref name=":4" /> Members of this cohort often [[Code-switching|code-switch]], "[aging] up when speaking to [Millennials] and [aging] down when speaking to younger relatives."<ref name=":5">{{cite web |last=Lansom |first=Alicia |title=Too Old For Gen Z, Too Young For Millennials: Life As A Confused Zillennial |url=https://www.refinery29.com/en-gb/generation-zillennial |access-date=26 August 2023 |website=www.refinery29.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> They are seen as "cultural tastemakers", particularly in [[youth subculture]]s for both younger Millennials and older members of Generation Z.<ref name=":8">{{cite web |last=Siu |first=Antoinette |date=24 April 2023 |title=What marketers need to know about 'Generation Zennial,' from social media to buying habits |url=https://digiday.com/marketing/what-marketers-need-to-know-about-generation-zennial-from-social-media-to-buying-habits/ |access-date=26 August 2023 |website=Digiday |language=en-US}}</ref> Their creative content is marked by an emphasis on authenticity, relatability, and [[social consciousness]], rejecting curated programming typical of the Millennial generation.<ref name=":8" /> They have substantial control over [[internet meme]] culture, donning the moniker "meme lords".<ref name=":2" /> "They remember life before the internet (just about), but they also know how to navigate meme culture and social media codes" according to a news article from [[Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism|Reuters Institute]].<ref>{{cite web |date=14 June 2024 |title=How these three Zillennial media leaders approach management in multigenerational newsrooms {{!}} Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism |url=https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/news/how-these-three-zillennial-media-leaders-approach-management-multigenerational-newsrooms |access-date=14 August 2025 |website=reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref> Charlotte Hilton, from ''Reader's Digest,'' wrote that zillennials "are fluent in both sarcasm and memes" and that "they witnessed the dawn of influencer culture and probably tried to become one during quarantine".<ref>{{cite web |last=Andersen |first=Charlotte Hilton |date=30 May 2025 |title=What Generation Are You? Find Out in Our Guide to Generation Years and Names |url=https://www.rd.com/article/generation-years-and-names/ |access-date=26 September 2025 |website=Reader's Digest |language=en-US}}</ref>

Zillennials are cultural hybrids of both Millennials and Gen Z according to a definition from Power Thesaurus.<ref>[https://www.powerthesaurus.org/zillennial/definitions ZILLENNIAL Definition & Meaning – Explained]</ref> [[Abercrombie & Fitch]] noted a target demographic of 25 to 29-year olds in 2022 as having "a bit of both Gen Z and Millennial mentality".<ref name="Obolenskaya2022">{{cite web |last1=Obolenskaya |first1=Christina |date=24 October 2022 |title=Q&A: How Abercrombie rebranded on TikTok |url=https://www.insiderintelligence.com/content/q-a-how-abercrombie-rebranded-on-tiktok |access-date=24 October 2022 |website=[[eMarketer]] |language=en}}</ref> They rebranded between 2020 and 2022 to capitalize around what they perceived to be the micro-generation's ethos: fulfillment and [[self-actualization]].<ref name="Obolenskaya2022" /> The brand identified zillennials and their usage of [[TikTok]] as being a major cultural exporter.<ref name="Obolenskaya2022" />

| caption1          = [[Game Boy Advance]], popular handheld gaming device
| caption2          = [[Nintendo DS]], popular handheld gaming device with two screens
| alt1              = Gameboy Advance
| alt2              = Nintendo DS
}}

Many Zillennials are nostalgic for the popular culture and technology of the [[2000s|first decade of the 21st century]], such as the ''[[Harry Potter]]'' franchise,<ref name=":5"/> ''[[SpongeBob SquarePants]]'',<ref>[https://www.trillmag.com/culture/fashion/zillennials-understanding-the-generation-caught-between-millennials-and-gen-z/ Zillennials: Understanding the Generation Caught Between Millennials and Gen Z]</ref> [[Game Boy Advance]],<ref name="ForbesIndia">[https://www.forbesindia.com/article/lifes/neither-gen-z-nor-millennials-are-zillennials-a-thing/86615/1 Neither Gen Z nor Millennials, are Zillennials a thing?]</ref> [[Nintendo DS]],<ref name="Glamour"/> and other [[Disney Channel]] and [[Nickelodeon]] shows.<ref name=":4">{{cite web |last=Kaufman |first=Ana |date=18 May 2023 |title=Move over Millennials and Gen Z, there's a new generation in town: Meet Zillennials |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/2023/05/18/is-zillennial-a-real-thing/70207436007/ |access-date=26 August 2023 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":5"/>

Mia Galuppo, writing for ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'', said that many viewers of the live-action ''[[Lilo & Stitch (2025 film)|Lilo and Stitch]]'' were Zillennials. She noted that "nostalgia as entertainment, intentional or not, is nothing new. But it has not yet been fully exploited for the Zillennial age demographic, which is now one of the largest age groups in the US". Data collected by Disney and [[PostTrak]] showed that moviegoers between ages 25 and 34 made up 33 percent of the film's non-family audience.<ref>{{cite web | title='Lilo & Stitch' and the Power of Zillennial Nostalgia at the Movie Theater | website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] | date=27 May 2025 | url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/lilo-and-stitch-and-the-power-of-zillennial-nostalgia-1236231230/ }}</ref>

Author Benjamin Crace, in his book titled ''The American Blockbuster: Movies That Defined Their Generations'', says that zillennials "have grown up with a steady dose of the supernatural in [[Popular culture|pop culture]] (vampires, witches, zombies) to a point where it has become somewhat normalized".<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WwXHEAAAQBAJ&dq=The+American+Blockbuster:+Movies+That+Defined+Their+Generations+zillennials&pg=PT209 | isbn=979-8-216-18418-8 | title=The American Blockbuster: Movies That Defined Their Generations | date=18 October 2022 | publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing USA }}</ref>

A 2024 report made by Parrot Analytics, a leading global entertainment analytics company, says that "the share of shows with strongly Zennial skewing audiences sometimes tracks more closely with Gen Z and sometimes with Millennials which can make it difficult to tease out unique content tastes for this cohort" but that they are particularly fond of [[Romance film|romantic movies]] (31%) over animated, horror and [[western film]]s.<ref>{{cite web |title=What are the most loved movie genres for each generation? |url=https://www.parrotanalytics.com/insights/movie-genre-preferences-each-generation-millennials-genz-genx/ |access-date=20 August 2025 |website=Parrot Analytics |language=en}}</ref>

Chris Molanphy, writing for [[Slate (magazine)|''Slate'']], said that [[Justin Bieber]], [[Miley Cyrus]], and [[Ariana Grande]] are a "tier of Millennial-slash-Z cuspers well past a decade of hitmaking and still scoring giant hits".<ref>{{cite news |last=Molanphy |first=Chris |date=24 January 2026 |title=One Generation Is Showing More Longevity on the Charts Than Any Before |url=https://slate.com/culture/2026/01/bruno-mars-billboard-hot-100-i-just-might-song.html |access-date=28 January 2026 |work=Slate |language=en-US |issn=1091-2339}}</ref>

=== Economic activity ===
Their outlook on their economic prospects was shaped by the decade's period of instability such as the [[Great Recession]] of the late 2000s and the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] beginning in 2020 and continuing into the early 2020s.<ref name="Napoli2020" /> Experiencing the effect of these crises on their parents, siblings, and others informed their outlook later on in life.<ref name=":2" /> Around 48% of American zillennials lived with their parents in 2023, which, coupled with their digital literacy and stable incomes, generates substantial [[Consumption (economics)|spending power]].<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Hartmans |first=Avery |title=Meet the 'zillennials,' who grew up online, live with their parents, and have retailers chasing their disposable income |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/zillennial-lives-with-parents-spends-on-luxury-goods-2023-1 |access-date=26 August 2023 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> An analysis by [[Morgan Stanley]] found that members of this cohort helped sustain the [[Luxury goods|luxury good sector]] during periods of economic downturn.<ref name=":7" /> In 2023, fund manager [[Ken Costa]] in a book review via the ''[[Financial Times]]'' argued that the transfer of wealth valued at $100&nbsp;trillion from Baby Boomers to younger generations, including zillennials, could restructure the global economy.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Alim |first=Arjun Neil |date=23 August 2023 |title=The transfer of wealth from boomers to 'zennials' will reshape the global economy |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/63027e28-724a-40bc-a929-7dec5125926c |access-date=26 August 2023}}</ref>

A report from [[Bank of America]] found in 2020 that zillennials carry outsized influence in financial markets due to their shifting consumer preferences away from "meat, alcohol and cars".<ref>{{cite news |last=Ossinger |first=Joanna |date=19 November 2020 |title=Zillennials Are Going to Change Investing Forever, BofA Says |language=en |work=Bloomberg.com |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-11-19/-zillennials-are-going-to-change-investing-forever-bofa-says |access-date=25 August 2023}}</ref> Payment processing researcher ''PYMNTS'' conducted a study on this cohort of US consumers in 2023.<ref name=":6">{{cite web |date=19 March 2023 |title=Zillennials Live Differently Than Millennials and Merchants See Dollar Signs |url=https://www.pymnts.com/consumer-insights/2023/zillennials-live-differently-than-millennials-and-merchants-see-dollar-signs/ |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=PYMNTS}}</ref> They are nearly identical to Generation Z when it comes to work habits, preferring similar levels of [[remote work]], social connection, and app platform usage.<ref name=":6" /> They grew up during the tail end of the 2000s hustle-culture that prioritised career success, while also being influenced by their Gen Z peers' more relaxed approach to work. They hold a dual citizenship of sorts.<ref>{{cite web |date=14 June 2024 |title=How these three Zillennial media leaders approach management in multigenerational newsrooms {{!}} Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism |url=https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/news/how-these-three-zillennial-media-leaders-approach-management-multigenerational-newsrooms |access-date=15 August 2025 |website=reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>

According to Mike Wiseman, writing for ''Personnel Today'', the UK's leading free-access HR website, Zillennials "overwhelmingly prefer working in an office but demand environments that justify the effort to get there. They expect their workspace to offer access to green spaces, lots of light, fresh air, wellness and leisure facilities, great restaurants with health-conscious menus, and culture". He added, "Zillennials are reluctant to waste unnecessary time commuting long distances and are put off by sterile, soulless corporate environments. They want a straightforward route to the office, on foot, bike or ideally one form of public transport".<ref>{{cite web |last=Wiseman |first=Mike |date=16 April 2025 |title=Exploring the best London office locations for 'Zillennials' |url=https://www.personneltoday.com/hr/exploring-the-best-london-office-locations-for-zillennials/ |access-date=26 December 2025 |website=Personnel Today |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Zillennials have higher [[brand loyalty]] and less [[Price elasticity of demand|price sensitivity]] than Millennials, leading to more stable purchasing patterns.<ref name=":8" /> According to ''PYMNTS'' Intelligence reports, 75% of zillennials shop both online and in-store, blending digital convenience with the tactile benefits of physical stores<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pymnts.com/news/retail/2025/75percent-zillennials-shop-online-in-store/ | title=75% of Zillennials Shop Both Online and In-Store | date=13 February 2025 }}</ref> and 72% of them are more influenced by trusted sources like friends or family than by traditional advertising when it comes to what drives their purchasing decisions.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pymnts.com/consumer-insights/2025/72percent-of-zillennials-trust-recommendations-more-than-ads-when-shopping/ | title=72% of Zillennials Trust Recommendations More Than Ads when Shopping | date=5 February 2025 }}</ref> Zillennials are discerning shoppers, many place a high value on social and environmental factors when picking where to shop.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Zillennial Paradox: Big Debt, Big Spending and a Conscience to Rule It All |url=https://www.pymnts.com/study_posts/the-zillennial-paradox-big-debt-big-spending-and-a-conscience-to-rule-it-all/ |access-date=18 August 2025 |website=PYMNTS.com |language=en-US}}</ref> For them, budgeting is also a key priority when making decisions about where and how to shop.<ref name="PYMNTS">{{cite web |last=PYMNTS |date=28 May 2024 |title=Spending Management Is Top of Mind for 'Zillennial' Shoppers |url=https://www.pymnts.com/consumer-insights/2024/spending-management-is-top-of-mind-for-zillennial-shoppers/ |access-date=9 November 2025 |website=PYMNTS.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

Consumers in this age group are more likely to live paycheck to paycheck than the population overall. Plus, they are likelier to have outstanding balances from student loans, credit cards, store cards and personal loans, among others.<ref name="PYMNTS"/>

A 2025 online survey of 1,089 US adults conducted by Arrivia, a travel loyalty technology provider, found that zillennials are emerging as a high-potential audience, with growing income and specific travel preferences. Nearly half live at home with their parents (48%) while reporting household incomes of $100,000 or more (41%), giving them more flexibility to spend on travel. Compared to the survey average, zillennials are nearly twice as likely to travel internationally. They also showed a higher interest than both Gen Z and Millennials in bundled packages that include a cruise, hotel and airfare. Nearly one in three zillennials (27%) said they've taken a cruise, compared to just 18% of Baby Boomers.<ref>{{cite web |title=New arrivia report finds growing cruise interest among zillennials |url=https://www.seatrade-cruise.com/marketing/new-arrivia-report-finds-growing-cruise-interest-among-zillennials |access-date=2026-06-20 |website=Seatrade Cruise News |language=en}}</ref><ref>https://resources.arrivia.com/hubfs/Reports/arrivia%20-%20Report%20-%20Loyalty%20and%20the%20Changing%20Traveler%20Q2%202025.pdf?hsLang=en</ref>

Zillennials are less likely than older consumers to own a motor vehicle as their primary means of transportation, instead, they are embracing alternatives such as leasing, public transit, and ridesharing services. They are also more likely than any other generation to name the lack of [[down payment]] funds as their top obstacle to home ownership.<ref>{{cite web |last=PYMNTS |date=19 March 2025 |title=59% of Zillennials Value Leasing as Vehicle Purchase Option |url=https://www.pymnts.com/consumer-insights/2025/59percent-of-zillennials-value-leasing-as-vehicle-purchase-option/ |access-date=14 November 2025 |website=PYMNTS.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Health ===
The onset of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] disrupted certain [[social marker]]s for zillennials.<ref>{{cite web |last=Williams |first=Jim |date=10 May 2023 |title=Zillennials: A new name for a generation |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TiCLP1JhURk |access-date=23 August 2023 |website=CBS Chicago}}</ref> They are less likely than Generation Z to use [[Online pharmacy|online pharmacies]].<ref name=":62">{{cite web |date=19 March 2023|title=Zillennials Live Differently Than Millennials and Merchants See Dollar Signs|url=https://www.pymnts.com/consumer-insights/2023/zillennials-live-differently-than-millennials-and-merchants-see-dollar-signs/|access-date=23 August 2023|website=PYMNTS}}</ref>

A ''PYMNTS'' Intelligence's Generational Pulse survey shows that "digital-first Gen Zers and zillennials are racing ahead on [[Telehealth|virtual doctor's visits]], health tracking apps, with alternative payment methods".<ref>{{cite web|title=Clicks, Care & Copays—How Each Generation Navigates Digital Healthcare|url=https://www.pymnts.com/study_posts/clicks-care-copays-how-each-generation-navigates-digital-healthcare/|website=PYMNTS.com|access-date=31 January 2026|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Personal values ===
According to [[CNN]], zillennials are more aligned with [[Political views of Generation Z|Generation Z on social issues]].<ref name=":3" /> A 2017 analysis by Ubl, Walden, and Arbit found that they were raised by "skeptical Xers and pragmatic [[Generation Jones|Gen Jonesers]]" who, in turn, instilled in them a preference for pragmatism to idealism.<ref name="UblWalden2017" /> Diversity and independence are the traits used most often by the cohort to describe what will set their micro-generation apart.<ref name="Dreisinger2019" /> The study found the cohort to be more creative and more likely to self-identify into a [[minority group]] than other generational cohorts.<ref name="Dreisinger2019" />

Zillennials believe in [[Climate change|global warming]] and efforts to [[Climate change mitigation|mitigate climate change]], with many identifying as eco-conscious.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Nadeem |first=Reem |date=26 May 2021 |title=Gen Z, Millennials Stand Out for Climate Change Activism, Social Media Engagement With Issue |url=https://www.pewresearch.org/science/2021/05/26/gen-z-millennials-stand-out-for-climate-change-activism-social-media-engagement-with-issue/ |access-date=25 August 2023 |website=Pew Research Center Science & Society |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Political activity ===
Patrice Peck, writing for ''[[Cosmopolitan (magazine)|Cosmopolitan]],'' stated that zillennials were between the ages of 18 and 29 during the [[2020 United States elections]], and were the "key to ousting then-president [[Donald Trump]] and sending [[Joe Biden]] and [[Kamala Harris]] to the White House".<ref name="Peck2022">{{cite web |last=Peck |first=Patrice |date=30 September 2022 |title=2022 Midterms Guide: The 7 Key States Where Zillennials Have the Power to Sway the Vote |url=https://www.cosmopolitan.com/politics/a41299314/2022-midterms-guide/ |access-date=12 November 2022 |website=[[Cosmopolitan (magazine)|Cosmo]] |language=en}}</ref> [[Glamour (magazine)|''Glamour UK'']] noted their general political outlook as more [[Socialism|socialist]] than Millennials.<ref name="Glamour">{{cite web |last=Quirk |first=Molly |date=12 August 2021 |title=I'm a 'Zillennial' – the limbo generation between Millennials and Gen Z – and this is what it's like to be too old for one; too young for the other |url=https://www.glamourmagazine.co.uk/article/zillennial-generation |access-date=25 August 2023 |website=Glamour UK |language=en-GB}}</ref> The [[2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum|UK Brexit referendum]] and [[2016 United States presidential election|US presidential election]], both occurring in 2016, are seen as key formative political events by zillennials, many of whom were not yet of voting age but who observed these events as they unfolded and were shaped by them.<ref name="Napoli2020" />

Zillennials actively participated in the [[George Floyd protests|2020–2021 George Floyd protests]] which were the largest series of protests against [[police brutality]] in the United States (alongside international protests) since the [[civil rights movement]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/2020/06/02/george-floydprotestersmillennials/5313474002/ |title=The faces of protesters are mostly millennials: Who are they and what do they think? |work=Cincinnati Enquirer |last=Haselhorst |first=Sarah |date=2 June 2020 |access-date=29 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The nation's racial justice protests are a pivotal moment for millennials and Gen Z |url=https://www.brookings.edu/articles/the-nations-racial-justice-protests-are-a-pivotal-moment-for-millennials-and-gen-z/ |access-date=21 February 2024 |website=Brookings |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Russonello |first=Giovanni |date=5 June 2020 |title=Why Most Americans Support the Protests |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/05/us/politics/polling-george-floyd-protests-racism.html |access-date=21 February 2024 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Pandemic helps 'Generation Z' ignite a movement |url=https://www.ft.com/content/effbfc03-61f3-4f99-910c-8befe46a6c08 |access-date=21 February 2024 |website=www.ft.com|date=12 June 2020 |last1=Weaver |first1=Courtney |last2=Manson |first2=Katrina }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=13 October 2020 |title=Are we 'Generation Screwed'? Not necessarily: coming of age amid COVID-19 |url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/magazine/article/are-we-generation-screwed-not-necessarily-coming-of-age-amid-covid-19 |access-date=21 February 2024 |website=Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

=== Social life ===
Zillennials are less likely than Generation Z to use digital means, such as text messaging and [[dating app]]s, to connect with a romantic partner.<ref name=":6" /> They are considered socially and [[Emotional intelligence|emotionally intelligent]].<ref name=":2" />

=== Technology ===
''[[USA Today]]'' described zillennials as being [[digital native]]s "steeped in [[internet culture]]" with high levels of [[digital literacy]].<ref name=":4"/> Zillennials and Generation Z share nearly identical digital engagement levels, 58.8% compared to 63.2%, respectively.<ref name=":6" /> Zillennials are more likely to consume news via online channels and play video games on [[Video game console|consoles]] than Generation Z.<ref name=":6" /> According to a study done by [[Fullscreen (company)|Fullscreen]], while zillennials are comfortable with technology and social media, they acknowledge it as a "love-hate relationship" with both.<ref name="Dreisinger2019" /> A majority of this cohort believe that technology betters the world.<ref name="Dreisinger2019" /> According to a 2024 report made by ''PYMNTS'', 68% of zillennials are using voice technology for daily tasks, they say that "this microgeneration uses [[Virtual assistant|voice assistants]] more frequently than older age groups, particularly in areas like shopping, financial management and obtaining information".<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pymnts.com/artificial-intelligence-2/2025/68-percent-of-zillennials-use-voice-technology-for-daily-tasks/ | title=68% of Zillennials Use Voice Technology for Daily Tasks | date=24 February 2025 }}</ref> Another report from the same company reveals that zillennials are a driving force behind the evolution of [[digital banking]], with a unique blend of tech-savviness and reliance on traditional financial institutions.<ref>{{cite web |last=PYMNTS |date=29 April 2025 |title=66% of Zillennials Use Their Phones as Bank Branch |url=https://www.pymnts.com/digital-first-banking/2025/66-percent-of-zillennials-use-their-phones-as-bank-branch/ |access-date=16 August 2025 |website=PYMNTS.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

According to authors Hannah Ubl, Lisa Walden, and Debra Arbit, what really divides Millennial/Gen Edge (Gen Z) cuspers from the Millennial bunch is their use of technology and social media, "while Millennials may pride themselves on their know-how of social media, the Millennial/Edger cuspers are social media mavens".<ref>{{cite book | last1=Ubl | first1=Hannah L. | last2=Walden | first2=Lisa X. | last3=Arbit | first3=Debra |title=Managing Millennials for Dummies |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=g36gDgAAQBAJ&dq=hannah+ubl+Managing+Millennials+For+Dummies+millennial/gen+edge+cusper&pg=PA266 |access-date=24 September 2025| date=6 April 2017 | publisher=John Wiley & Sons | isbn=978-1-119-31023-5 }}</ref>
